policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the verb causatively with a personal object, "drove out the Amorites that were there", which is the hiphil sense of the qere וַיּוֹרֶשׁ (dispossess/drive out). The ketiv ויירש, with its doubled yod, points to the qal wayyiras, which ASV elsewhere gives as "possessed"; "drove out" is not that verb's rendering. No ASV note is mapped to this unit, but the wording alone distinguishes the reading.
